s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of joint pain and swelling following medical treatment for a gynecological condition
salient_findings: Diffuse swelling and tenderness to palpation of both knees
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
key_facts: 6 weeks of amenorrhea
Right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Vaginal bleeding
Empty uterine cavity on transvaginal ultrasonography
Gestational sac in the right adnexa without fetal cardiac activity
Initial serum β-hCG level of 585 mIU/mL
Decline in β-hCG level after methotrexate administration
Pain and swelling in both knees after methotrexate treatment
Diffuse swelling and tenderness to palpation of both knees
Elevated white-cell count
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate
Elevated C-reactive protein level
Joint ultrasonography revealed anterior soft-tissue swelling with a thickened synovium and fluid collections

shortlist.label: Reactive arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of joint pain and swelling following medical treatment for a gynecological condition, consistent with reactive arthritis triggered by a recent infection or medical intervention

shortlist.label: Methotrexate-induced rheumatologic reaction
shortlist.why_kept: Recent methotrexate administration and subsequent development of joint pain and swelling, suggesting a possible methotrexate-induced reaction

shortlist.label: Septic arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Acute onset of joint pain and swelling, with elevated white-cell count and C-reactive protein level, raising concern for septic arthritis

shortlist.label: Seronegative spondyloarthropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Presentation of joint pain and swelling, with elevated inflammatory markers, consistent with seronegative spondyloarthropathy

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Symmetric joint involvement and elevated inflammatory markers, although less likely given the acute onset and recent medical treatment

raw.rationale: The patient developed knee pain and swelling shortly after receiving methotrexate, which is a known side effect of the medication, and the lack of fever and unremarkable radiographs make other diagnoses less likely

rejected.label: Reactive arthritis
rejected.why: No clear evidence of recent gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection

rejected.label: Septic arthritis
rejected.why: The patient was afebrile and the laboratory tests did not indicate a clear infection

rejected.label: Seronegative spondyloarthropathy
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are acute and limited to the knees, without evidence of chronic disease or other typical features

rejected.label: Rheumatoid arthritis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms are acute and do not meet the typical criteria for rheumatoid arthritis, which usually includes symmetric joint involvement and positive serology
